subject: Human Evolution
title: Handedness and the Brain
description: A micro-lesson that makes Handedness and the Brain usable.

hook.text: About 90% of humans are right-handed. No other species shows such a strong population-level bias.

buildup.text: Handedness reflects brain lateralization: the left hemisphere controls the right hand and language.

discovery.text: Flake scars on ancient tools reveal the knapper's dominant hand—right-handedness goes back 1.8 million years.

twist.text: Lateralization may have freed brain space: one side for sequences, the other for spatial reasoning.

climax.text: The same neural wiring that gave us a dominant hand also gave us structured language and tool grammar.

punchline.text: Your dominant hand is proof of a lopsided brain.

quiz.question: What does handedness in ancient hominins suggest?
options: Brain lateralization linked to tool use and language
